text:
Elena (Finance): Meterly just sent a renewal + an invoice for last month with unexpected 'processing surcharge'. Renewal list is +16%. Can procurement validate the invoice and run an alternative compare against CostGauge?

Ravi (Billing): I pulled the invoice; surcharge code MT-PROC-2025 shows $8,750. Our exported CSV doesn't include that line. Opening a billing dispute with Meterly.

Noel (Procurement): Do not sign renewal until dispute is resolved. I'll request an itemized breakdown and metadata for that surcharge. Also will ask CostGauge for a back-of-envelope TCO using our usage.

Tori (Platform): Integration note: Meterly pushes hourly JSON exports to our S3 prefix and we run the reconcile job. CostGauge advertises delta webhooks which could cut our reconciliation Lambda time ~15%. Need to see the webhook schema and rate limits.

Marta (Legal): Before sharing any raw usage with CostGauge, they must sign our NDA + DPA. Also request SOC2 Type II and subprocessors list. No migration until DPA in place.

Ravi (Billing): Action: I'll export last 12 months by sku and post sanitized CSV to #finance-data. Sample rows:

```
month,sku,events_processed,bytes_exported
2024-07,billable_events,98234,234567890
2024-08,billable_events,110987,276543210
```

Ravi (Billing): CSV ETA: 2h.

Noel (Procurement): I'll draft an RFP template for Meterly and CostGauge: base, per-event, retention, egress, onboarding credit, backfill pricing, SLA credits, termination rights. Also ask for a 12mo vs 24mo pricing table.

vendor-bot: Meterly uploaded invoice_1779123600.pdf and provisional_renewal_1779123620.pdf. Renewal list: $35,000/mo -> proposed $40,600/mo.

Elena (Finance): Target negotiation: ask for 15% off list or 9 months at current rate + 3 months free on a 12mo commit. Also request a one-time migration credit if we switch.

Noel (Procurement): I'll push for the migration credit and require they not bill disputed items while we review. If Meterly won't budge, we'll pilot CostGauge on a narrow namespace for 30 days before any cutover.

Tori (Platform): If CostGauge webhooks match our event fields (event_id,timestamp,sku,qty) we can spin a sandbox POC in 10 business days. Otherwise plan for a two-week ETL to adapt schemas.

Marta (Legal): I'll pre-draft our DPA checklist and send to Procurement. Include export format, deletion windows, breach notice timing, and right-to-audit.

Ravi (Billing): Uploaded the sanitized 12mo CSV to #finance-data. Link: https://redwood.s3/finance-data/meterly_usage_12mo.csv (internal).

Noel (Procurement): Sending the RFP to both vendors in 48h. Will attach the sanitized usage under NDA.

Elena (Finance): Great. Next steps: confirm Meterly dispute outcome, RFP out in 48h, CostGauge reply in ~72h. Reconvene in 4 days to review responses. /remind me 4 days
